title: Home Made Food service
answer: The Home Made Food section lets users discover food cooked by local home cooks. Users can search for cooks, cuisines or dishes and browse what is available near them.

title: Searching and filtering food
answer: In the Home Made Food section, users can search for cooks, cuisines, or dishes, and apply filters to narrow down the results before choosing what to order.

title: What food listings show
answer: Each home cook listing displays information such as ratings, reviews, preparation time, location, cuisine type, food categories, and popular dishes, along with the cook's menu.

title: Example home cooks on MAA
answer: Example home cooks shown in the MAA interface include Aiza Aunty, Adeel Bhai, and Mubeen Didi. These are demo examples of the kind of local home cooks featured on the platform.

title: Why Home Made Food matters emotionally
answer: Home Made Food is designed to trigger nostalgia and comfort. It reminds users of home cooked meals, which is especially useful for students and people living away from their families.

title: Home Made Food module structure
answer: The Home Made Food module covers cook listing, search, filters, ratings, menus, and general food discovery for users browsing the platform.

title: The kind of home cooked dishes featured
answer: Home Made Food is meant to feature everyday South Asian home cooking, comfort dishes like daal, karahi, biryani or pulao, kebabs, and roti or naan, the kind of meals someone would normally get at home rather than at a restaurant, prepared with simpler, homely ingredients.
source: food.txt + research: South Asian home cooking

title: Why MAA asks if you have eaten
answer: In many South Asian households, asking whether someone has eaten is one of the most common ways care is shown, more a way of checking in than a literal question about food. Talk to MAA and the Home Made Food section both lean into this, treating food as a form of care, not just a transaction.

source: research: food-as-love-language, South Asian family culture

title: Comfort food examples for a bad day
answer: For someone feeling low, tired, or unwell, warm comfort dishes like daal chawal, chicken soup style shorba, or khichdi are commonly turned to as gentle, easy-to-digest home cooked meals, similar to how these dishes are used in South Asian households.
source: research: South Asian comfort food traditions
